title: STP Imaging Protocol
author: Katie Matho
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.sqcedsw

steps.title: Prepare Raw Imaging Data
steps.instruction: Organize and clean the raw serial two-photon tomography (STPT) data before processing.

substeps.instruction: Verify that all sections (.tiff) are saved in both ch1 (red channel) and ch2 (green channel).
Remove ch3 (blank channel) tiffs acquisition data using the 'move_test.bat' script.
Transfer ch1 and ch2 raw data to the IBM SONAS server.

steps.title: Set Up Processing Scripts
steps.instruction: Configure the processing environment and reconstruction scripts on the processing server.

substeps.instruction: Create a process folder with the project ID in the processing server (e.g., /data/<user>/STP_processed_data/<cell_type>/<group>/).
Copy the reconstruction script into the process folder.
Edit the 'runReconstruction_part1.sh' script using gedit to input relevant data paths.
Update the Mosaic text file located in the ch1 raw data folder.
Update the CH2_TIF_DIR and CH3_TIF_DIR paths.
Update SECTION_STARTNUMBER and SECTION_ENDNUMBER (e.g., 270) based on the imaging data.
Verify advanced parameters are set to default: IMAGE_CORRECTION=1 and FUSION_METHOD=4 (no blending).

steps.title: Execute Image Reconstruction
steps.instruction: Run the reconstruction script to stitch image tiles into coronal sections.

substeps.instruction: Open the Terminal and change the directory to the processed data folder.
Run the reconstruction script from the Terminal.

steps.title: Perform Image Reconstruction Quality Control
steps.instruction: Verify the quality of the reconstructed images and the folder structure.

substeps.instruction: Visualize stitched images in Fiji to check overall acquisition quality.
Confirm the presence of 'stitchedImage_ch1' and 'stitchedImage_ch2' folders (1 µm resolution, 50 µm spacing, LZW compressed 16-bit tif).
Check the 'warping' folder for 5% downsized images for quick visualization.
Review the 'Log' folder for missing tiles information.

steps.title: Implement Signal Detection Networks
steps.instruction: Use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) on a CUDA-enabled GPU to detect cells and axons.

substeps.instruction: Select the appropriate network ID: 164 (c-fos/nuclear), 10 (Mecp2-GFP/intra-nuclear), 313 (subtraction channel c-fos/nuclear), or 320 (Rabies/Somatic labeling).
Identify the anterior commissure region in the stitched images.
Use MATLAB to calculate the image intensity mean and standard deviation of the anterior commissure region for both channels.
Determine the warpable range of the stitched brain by comparing start and end coordinates against the 25 micron Allen reference atlas.
Input these values and the channel directories into the prediction script and run predictions.

steps.title: Register Data to CCF Space
steps.instruction: Register the downsampled sample brain to the Common Coordinated Framework (CCF) space using a two-step process (affine followed by b-spline registration) via the elastix toolbox.

steps.title: Perform Detection and Registration Quality Control
steps.instruction: Qualitatively assess the accuracy of cell masks and registration.

substeps.instruction: Open cell mask images alongside reconstructed sections in Fiji using a synchronized mouse pointer to assess detection quality.
Open the registration result file in the 'elastixOutput' folder in 'warping' alongside the fixed downsized warpable image; synchronize slices and pointers to check for congruous edges and corners.

steps.title: Calculate Region-Wise Cell Counts
steps.instruction: Transform detected cell coordinates to CCF space to determine counts per brain region using C++ and R code.

substeps.instruction: Create a Project folder in the processing server containing designated groups for brains and the MATLAB script.
Organize point list text files into appropriate groups (e.g., Group 1 for female, Group 2 for male).
Run the MATLAB script 'runROI_all' on the processing server.
Extract summary text files for both hemispheres from the output folder and copy them into a spreadsheet (.csv) for visualization.

steps.title: Compress Data for Archival
steps.instruction: Compress raw STPT data for R24 archival to reduce storage requirements.

substeps.instruction: Run the compression script on the processing server (CPU-intensive, no GPU required).
Document the raw data size before compression (~145 GB) and after compression (~65-75 GB).
Optional: Convert Level 1 reconstructed images to JP2 format or compress Level 2 cell masks as binary tif images.
